discoveries: (a) `gov check`'s runner keeps only the first 200 characters of a check's output (`src/gov/check/runner.py:153`, a file this ticket doesn't change). In the no-store project the context's message ends with the temporary path, so the refusal carries `context-reproducibility: cannot read the store or the ticket folder: .gov-runtime/store.db: no store at /tmp/…` cut short, and never STORE_MISSING or the full message. (b) Besides the check, the context-failure refusals carry the context's reason word for word, for example `ERROR: PROJ-ctxf: mandatory input 'DEC-old' is superseded and cannot satisfy a current requirement`. The superseded-source projects are also RED at core-authority (`SUPERSEDED_SATISFYING_REQUIREMENT`, and `FRONTMATTER_UNREADABLE: .tickets/PROJ-ctxf.md: the frontmatter writes a key twice`). The duplicate key looks like a fixture artefact of `build_ticket(sources=…)` on top of the ticket template's default `sources`. I didn't touch it; it doesn't change any outcome. (c) The no-store project is also RED at recovery-rebuild. (d) The repair ticket is named under `details.repair_ticket` (for example `pro-1smb`).
risks: Case [6] now also accepts the reason's stem (`<store>: no store`) because `gov check` cuts the full message at 200 characters. The original two alternatives are kept and the stem is the context's reason as the check gives it, but it is a narrower match than the full message: please look at it if that stem reads as a lowered expectation. The telling-test pattern is round 2's; I didn't separately show that `test_told.py` tells when a close does run tests (it sits in the ticket's acceptance folder, which the close runs). Part 1 of W1-30 ran above the load ceiling (green all the same).
